## vllm:lora_requests_info leaks a series per observed adapter-set state

I run 8×TP2 pods serving 200 LoRA adapters and noticed the llm-d router
(the downstream metrics consumer) intermittently dropping healthy pods from
its scheduling pool during benchmarks. Chasing that led here.

The gauge encodes the current running/waiting adapter sets in its *labels*:

```python
self.gauge_lora_info.labels(**lora_info_labels).set_to_current_time()
```

prometheus_client keeps every distinct label combination exposed forever,
and nothing ever removes the previous child. So every time a request starts
or finishes and the in-flight set changes, that exact (running, waiting)
pair becomes a permanent series in /metrics. With 200 adapters the churn is
combinatorial. From the Prometheus data I collected during a 5 minute
benchmark on v0.31.0:

```
t=   0s:    1 series
t=  60s:  291 series
t= 140s: 1352 series
after 5 min: 4451 series   # for this one gauge
```

The exposition grows until scrapes slow down enough that the router (1s
refresh, 2s staleness threshold) starts considering pods stale and filters
them out of the candidate set. While all 8 pods were healthy and Ready:

```
candidate sizes: {1: 26, 2: 20, 4: 15, 5: 6, 8: 24}   # 91 requests
```

74% of requests were scheduled against a shrunken pool, which is what
broke the adapter-affinity routing (session bindings kept migrating as
their bound pod flapped in and out).

## The fix

Remember the last label values per engine and `remove()` the previous
child when the set changes, so the exposition holds only the current
state. Per-engine so DP engines don't delete each other's children.
Ray gauges have no child series to remove, so `RayGaugeWrapper` gained a
no-op `remove()` to keep the gauge API the same; Ray deployments behave as
before.

One series per engine is the correct steady state — this is a
current-state gauge, not a history log. Prometheus already keeps history:
each state change is its own time series there, and consumers are expected
to pick the latest (the llm-d router sorts by the gauge value, which is the
state's refresh timestamp).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| series in exposition | unbounded (4451 measured) | 1 per engine |
| scrape size | grows forever | constant |
| stale series in Prometheus | flatlined forever | marked stale in 5 min |
| healthy pods dropped by staleness-sensitive routers | yes (measured) | no |

## Workaround

Until this lands, I run the router (llm-d EPP) with
`--metrics-staleness-threshold=30s` so transiently slow scrapes don't evict
healthy pods from the scheduling candidate pool. That masks the routing
symptom but doesn't stop the exposition from growing.

## Testing

New unit tests in `tests/v1/metrics/test_lora_requests_info.py` covering
accumulation, current-state exposure, per-engine isolation, shared label
sets between engines, and the no-lora-config case.

`test_lora_requests_info_does_not_accumulate_series` fails on unpatched
v0.31.0 and passes with the fix; all 5 pass in a v0.31.0-based container.

```release-note
Fix unbounded prometheus series accumulation in `vllm:lora_requests_info`
when serving LoRA adapters: the previous label set is now removed when the
running/waiting adapter sets change, keeping the `/metrics` exposition at
one series per engine.
```

To answer the question: removing a label set that is no longer present is a no-op in prometheus_client (`dict.pop` with a default), so a stale removal cannot raise. The shared-label case between engines was real though — an update by one engine could drop the series another engine still held. @@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the vllm:lora_requests_info series lifecycle."""
+
+import pytest
+from prometheus_client import REGISTRY
+
+from vllm.config import DeviceConfig, LoRAConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.v1.metrics.loggers import PrometheusStatLogger
+from vllm.v1.metrics.prometheus import unregister_vllm_metrics
+from vllm.v1.metrics.stats import SchedulerStats
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+TEST_MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B"
+METRIC_NAME = "vllm:lora_requests_info"
+
+
+def build_logger_config(lora_config: LoRAConfig | None = None) -> VllmConfig:
+    return VllmConfig(
+        model_config=ModelConfig(model=TEST_MODEL),
+        device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cuda"),
+        lora_config=lora_config,
+    )
+
+
+def make_lora_config() -> LoRAConfig:
+    return LoRAConfig(max_loras=8)
+
+
+def lora_info_series() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    """Collect the exposed (running, waiting) label pairs of the gauge."""
+    found = []
+    for metric in REGISTRY.collect():
+        if metric.name != METRIC_NAME:
+            continue
+        for sample in metric.samples:
+            found.append(
+                (
+                    sample.labels["running_lora_adapters"],
+                    sample.labels["waiting_lora_adapters"],
+                )
+            )
+    return found
+
+
+def record_states(logger: PrometheusStatLogger, states: list[dict[str, int]]):
+    for state in states:
+        logger.record(SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters=state), None)
+
+
+def test_lora_requests_info_does_not_accumulate_series():
+    config = build_logger_config(make_lora_config())
+    try:
+        logger = PrometheusStatLogger(config)
+        states = [
+            {},
+            {"adapter-a": 1},
+            {"adapter-a": 1, "adapter-b": 2},
+            {"adapter-b": 1},
+            {},
+        ]
+        record_states(logger, states)
+        # Only the last state may remain exposed.
+        assert lora_info_series() == [("", "")]
+    finally:
+        unregister_vllm_metrics()
+
+
+def test_lora_requests_info_keeps_current_state():
+    config = build_logger_config(make_lora_config())
+    try:
+        logger = PrometheusStatLogger(config)
+        record_states(logger, [{"adapter-a": 1, "adapter-b": 1}])
+        assert lora_info_series() == [("adapter-a,adapter-b", "")]
+    finally:
+        unregister_vllm_metrics()
+
+
+def test_lora_requests_info_per_engine_children():
+    config = build_logger_config(make_lora_config())
+    try:
+        logger = PrometheusStatLogger(config, engine_indexes=[0, 1])
+        logger.record(
+            SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters={"adapter-a": 1}), None, engine_idx=0
+        )
+        logger.record(
+            SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters={"adapter-b": 1}), None, engine_idx=1
+        )
+        logger.record(
+            SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters={"adapter-c": 1}), None, engine_idx=0
+        )
+        assert sorted(lora_info_series()) == [("adapter-b", ""), ("adapter-c", "")]
+    finally:
+        unregister_vllm_metrics()
+
+
+def test_lora_requests_info_shared_label_between_engines():
+    """A shared state is only removed once the last engine holding it
+    moves on."""
+    config = build_logger_config(make_lora_config())
+    try:
+        logger = PrometheusStatLogger(config, engine_indexes=[0, 1])
+        shared = {"adapter-a": 1}
+        logger.record(SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters=shared), None, engine_idx=0)
+        logger.record(SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters=shared), None, engine_idx=1)
+        assert lora_info_series() == [("adapter-a", "")]
+
+        # engine 0 moves on — engine 1 still holds the shared state
+        logger.record(
+            SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters={"adapter-b": 1}), None, engine_idx=0
+        )
+        assert sorted(lora_info_series()) == [("adapter-a", ""), ("adapter-b", "")]
+
+        # engine 1 moves on too — now the shared state is removed
+        logger.record(
+            SchedulerStats(running_lora_adapters={"adapter-c": 1}), None, engine_idx=1
+        )
+        assert sorted(lora_info_series()) == [("adapter-b", ""), ("adapter-c", "")]
+    finally:
+        unregister_vllm_metrics()
+
+
+def test_lora_requests_info_absent_without_lora_config():
+    config = build_logger_config()
+    try:
+        logger = PrometheusStatLogger(config)
+        assert logger.gauge_lora_info is None
+        record_states(logger, [{"adapter-a": 1}])
+        assert lora_info_series() == []
+    finally:
+        unregister_vllm_metrics()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    pytest.main([__file__])
